title: Orthodontic Benefit Riders: Takeover Establishment Entries
content:
**Orthodontic Benefit Riders (Cascade Ortho Rider family): takeover establishment.**

## Cases established as new starts although banded before coverage began

When a case was established as a new start although its appliances were placed before coverage of the case began, Cascade does not refuse the case. Instead:

- it re-establishes the case as a takeover from the month coverage began;
- it does so with a takeover establishment entry under the same case number, which supersedes the new-start entry;
- on that entry it fixes the months of treatment still to come when coverage begins, and the fee it recognises for the treatment the rider covers.

Only such cases are re-established this way.

## Takeover cases from the start

A case established as a takeover from the start (treatment begun under another carrier or before the rider effective date) is covered when the rider allows takeovers and at least the rider's takeover minimum months of planned treatment remain on the rider effective date. The waiting period and age limit do not apply to such a takeover, but the lifetime maximum does.

A case re-established under this rule is not re-established when fewer than the rider's takeover minimum months of treatment are still to come when its coverage begins, or when the rider does not allow takeovers.

## What the takeover establishment entry shows

- **Months remaining:** the months of treatment still to come when coverage begins.
- **Origin:** takeover.
- **Kept from the new-start entry:** the case number, banding date, appliance, planned treatment months and treatment fee.
- **Network status and participation agreement:** those fixed for the practice now treating the patient on the date of the takeover entry. A Cascade PPO or Premier Participating Dentist Agreement in force with the orthodontist specialty gives in network; anything else gives out of network.

Afterwards the case history shows the takeover entry as the case's latest establishment. No payment is made or taken back by recording it.

## Recording the entry: `record_ortho_takeover_case_574129ed`

The agent unlocks the agent tool `record_ortho_takeover_case_574129ed` and then calls it. One call records a new establishment entry for the case with the takeover origin.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ortho_rider_id` | reference number of the patient's orthodontic rider, as returned by the orthodontic rider lookup for the subscriber | identifier |
| `ortho_case_event_id` | reference number of the establishment entry being superseded, as returned by the orthodontic case lookup for that rider | identifier |
| `provider_agreement_id` | reference number of the participation agreement in force for the practice now treating the patient on the date of the takeover entry, as returned by the provider agreement lookup | identifier; empty string when that practice holds no Cascade agreement |
| `network_status` | network status of the practice now treating the patient on the date of the takeover entry | `in_network` (it holds a Cascade PPO or Premier participating agreement in force that day with the orthodontist specialty) or `out_of_network` (otherwise) |
| `months_remaining` | months of planned treatment still to come when coverage of the case begins | whole number of months |
| `allowed_case_fee` | the fee Cascade recognises for the covered treatment | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent; stored as given |

**Receipt.** A successful call returns:

- the reference of the new takeover entry (`establishment_entry`);
- the case number;
- the case origin (always takeover);
- the network status;
- the months remaining;
- the recognised fee;
- the entry date.

A receipt carrying an establishment-entry reference means the case is now recorded as a takeover.
